title: fix(service-storage): a parent-record editor may delete another user's attachment
body:
Fixes #21729
Clause-②: yes (widening)

## What this changes

A member holding `org_member` who can edit a record may now delete another user's attachment on it. The attachment gate (`installAttachmentAccessHooks`, delete branch) has always declared this rule: the uploader OR a user who can edit the parent record. Before this PR, the platform's row-level delete floor in `member_default` (`owner_only_deletes`: `created_by == current_user.id`, positions `['org_member']`) refused the delete in the security middleware's by-id pre-image step (`security-plugin.ts`, the `PermissionDeniedError` of step 2.7). The gate's parent-editor branch was never reached.

This follows the maintainer's ruling A on the card (comment 5979859114): a delete-only alternate match, contributed TOGETHER with the gate that judges it.

- **The seam (`@objectstack/plugin-security`).** Before this PR, no plugin other than plugin-security could contribute a row policy. Permission sets resolve by name from metadata, the bootstrap list and `sys_permission_set`, and the human baseline is `member_default` plus an app `isDefault` set. The new method is `contributeOwnershipFloorAlternates(plugin, alternates)` on the registered `security` service. It extends `ISecurityService` the same way `getMetadataReadableFields` and `discardPermissionSetOverlay` do, so there is no `packages/spec` edit. Contributions are keyed by the contributing plugin: a second call replaces the first, and an empty list withdraws it. The seam throws on three kinds of contribution:
  - an object of `'*'`, which would withdraw the floor instead of relieving it;
  - an operation that is not one floor limb (`all`, `select`, `insert`);
  - a policy that does not parse as `RowLevelSecurityPolicySchema`.
- **Placement.** `collectRLSPolicies` puts each alternate beside every enabled shipped floor policy of its limb (`withOwnershipFloorAlternates`), and copies that floor policy's `positions`. The alternate therefore reaches exactly the principals the floor binds. It can only add an OR match to a write class the floor already occupies, so it can never make an empty write class non-empty. An empty write class is what triggers the derive-from-select rule, which is the reason `sys_comment_moderation`'s comment gives for its load-bearing domain. Each materialized alternate also carries the floor's provenance (`isPlatformOwnershipFloorPolicy`). Every composition that drops the floor drops its relief too, and `checkAuthoredRowWrite` never reads an alternate as an app-authored widener.
- **The contribution (`@objectstack/service-storage`).** `contributeAttachmentDeleteFloorAlternate` contributes `sys_attachment_parent_editor_delete` (`object: 'sys_attachment'`, `operation: 'delete'`, `using: 'id != null'`). Its domain is inherited from the floor: `['org_member']`. The call sits in the same `kernel:ready` branch that installs the gate, right after `installAttachmentAccessHooks`. Without the gate there is no relief. If the security service lacks the seam or refuses the contribution, the plugin logs it at `warn` and the floor stays in force (fail closed).
- **Not changed:** `owner_only_deletes`, `member_default`, the floor's edit limb, `attachment-access-hooks.ts`, and `packages/spec`.

## Measured at the door

Measured on an org-bound dogfood boot (`orgContext: true`, both members armed with `org_member` and the delete grant):

| caller, row | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| parent editor, not the uploader, `DELETE` | 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` (floor) | **200**, row gone |
| non-uploader who can READ but not EDIT the parent, `DELETE` | 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` (floor) | 403 `ATTACHMENT_DELETE_DENIED` (gate) |
| non-uploader who cannot READ the parent, `DELETE` | 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` (floor) | 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` (pre-image: the row is invisible to the caller) |
| parent editor, not the uploader, `PATCH` (edit limb) | 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` | 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`, row unchanged |
| boot WITHOUT service-storage (`SysAttachment` registered by a host plugin): parent editor `DELETE` / creator `DELETE` | n/a | 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` / 200 |

**One deviation from the expected pin, measured and kept.** The REST pin at case (a), memberB on the private `att_secret` parent, now asserts ONE code. That code is `PERMISSION_DENIED`, not `ATTACHMENT_DELETE_DENIED`. memberB cannot read that parent, so read visibility (`installAttachmentReadVisibility`) hides the attachment from them: its by-id GET answers 404. The pre-image re-read refuses a row the caller cannot see before the gate runs. The gate's refusal names the parent object and id, so this order also keeps them from a caller who cannot read that record. The gate's own code is pinned on a parent the caller CAN read (`att_readonly`): `ATTACHMENT_DELETE_DENIED`. Getting the gate's code for an invisible parent would mean bypassing read visibility in the pre-image, and would disclose the parent's identity.

## Pins

- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/attachments-permission-matrix.dogfood.test.ts` (declared cross-lane path, test only; no assertion deleted). The matrix boots org-bound with an `assertArmed` precondition. Before this PR it booted org-less, so the floor never applied and case (a) accepted "either" code. The case (a) assertion now checks one code. Three new cases cover the parent-editor 200, the readable non-editor `ATTACHMENT_DELETE_DENIED`, and the untouched edit limb. A new describe boots without service-storage.
- `plugin-security/src/ownership-floor-alternates.test.ts` covers the seam's refusals and plugin keying, and the placement beside the enabled shipped floor only, with floor provenance. It also checks **byte-identity**: on a real `SecurityPlugin`, every (principal × object × operation) cell's collected policies AND compiled filter are compared with and without the contribution. The principals are member, org-less, org admin and an MCP agent holding `org_member`. The objects are `sys_attachment`, `sys_comment` and an ordinary object. The operations are delete, update, find and insert. Exactly one cell moves: the member's `sys_attachment` delete. Withdrawing the contribution restores every cell.
- `service-storage`: `attachment-delete-floor-alternate.test.ts` covers the contribution and its no-security, no-seam and refused outcomes. `storage-service-plugin.test.ts` checks that the contribution happens exactly once and after the gate, and that nothing is contributed on an engine without a hook seam.

## Ablations

Each ablation was run through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` with a trap restore, a rebuild and `ablation-dist-preflight.mjs`. Each was restored, and the restore was proven: blob equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` is empty, the dist marker is back, and every pin is green again.

1. **Drop the contribution.** Prediction: two dogfood cells red, not one. Measured: 2 red. The parent-editor delete answered 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` instead of 200, and the readable non-editor answered `PERMISSION_DENIED` instead of `ATTACHMENT_DELETE_DENIED`. One storage wiring pin was also red. The other 17 dogfood cells stayed green, including the edit limb and the no-storage boot.
2. **Widen the alternate to `operation: 'all'`.** Prediction: the seam refuses it, so the result matches ablation 1 and the edit-limb pin stays green. Measured: the seam refused it ("is not one floor limb"), the same 2 dogfood cells were red, and the edit-limb pin was green. 2b, relieving the edit limb as well by contributing a second `update` alternate: only the edit-limb pin went red (PATCH answered 200).
3. **Drop the inherited domain in `withOwnershipFloorAlternates`.** Measured: the byte-identity pin went red. The cells that moved were the org-less principal's and the org admin's `sys_attachment` delete, the derive-from-select regression.

## Verification at `158aa1a3dd`

- **Gates:** `dispatch-gates --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --commands` derived 104 families, and all 104 exited 0. `dispatch-gates --ran` reports 104 accounted for and 0 NOT-MEASURED. Three gates needed work before passing:
  - `check:skill-examples` and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` first exited 3 (prerequisite: unbuilt dists). They are green after building those packages.
  - `check:engine-double-contract` was red once, on the new test's engine double. The fix routes `findOne` through `assertEngineFindOnePredicate` and records the ledger row.
- **Dogfood:** the attachments dogfood file passes 19 tests, with 1 skipped (block (g) is `skipIf` the organizations package is unavailable).
- **Package suites** (at `a90a609a20`; only a dogfood comment changed after it):
  - `@objectstack/service-storage` `test`: 42 files, 640 tests pass.
  - `@objectstack/plugin-security` `test`: 165 files, 3551 tests pass and 45 are skipped.
  - `typecheck` is clean for both packages and for `@objectstack/dogfood`.
- `pnpm lint` was not run locally; it is left to CI.

## Docs

`content/docs/permissions/attachments-access.mdx`: the delete section now names which refusal answers when, and says that the floor relief exists only where service-storage installs the gate. No `skills/**` sentence is made false. `skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md` still correctly recommends `owner_only_writes` / `owner_only_deletes`.

## Acceptance notes

- **Out of scope, reported to the seat to file (class a, a possible data leak).** This is a pre-existing problem and this PR neither touches nor widens it. A principal outside the floor's `org_member` domain can send a delete for an attachment whose parent it cannot read. The gate's delete-branch refusal (`ATTACHMENT_DELETE_DENIED`) then answers, not the platform's not-visible refusal, and that refusal names the parent record. Members inside the domain are unaffected: read visibility refuses first in the pre-image. The measurement is in the dev report on the card.
- The triage note said `sys_attachment` is "registered by platform-objects". Measured: it is DEFINED there and publicly exported (`@objectstack/platform-objects/audit`). In this repo it is REGISTERED only by service-storage's manifest. The ruling's concern still holds, because a host can register the exported object without the storage plugin. The new describe block does exactly that.
